mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, leading to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of strong GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, or the correlation between the federal funds rate and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when the unemployment rate is below 4%, or the correlation between the unemployment rate and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate a strong economy, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when housing starts exceed 1200 and the unemployment rate is below 5%, or the correlation between housing starts, unemployment rate, and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative during periods of strong industrial production growth, or the correlation between industrial production and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when the federal funds rate is below 4% and the money supply exceeds 350000, or the correlation between the federal funds rate, money supply, and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when payroll employment exceeds 140000, or the correlation between payroll employment and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index indicates decreased inflationary pressures, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when the consumer price index is below 200, or the correlation between the consumer price index and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).
